name: llmc_gpt2_forward
goal: Port gpt2_forward_harness.cu (llm.c's train_gpt2_fp32.cu, the fp32 GPT-2 training program, which it includes) to idiomatic SYCL 2020 with zero dpct helpers, computed on the SYCL device. Keep the program's contract: `build/candidate <debug_state.bin> <output> build/gpt2_124M.bin` loads the GPT-2 124M weights, runs a target-free forward pass on the debug batch and then one with its targets, and writes raw float32: the B*T*V logits (V per row, not the padded Vp), then the mean loss, exactly as the CUDA main does. A hidden reference checks the output against PyTorch's within 1e-2 absolute (llm.c's own test tolerance), so use precise math (sycl::exp, not native::exp). cuBLAS calls go to oneMath (oneapi::math::blas::column_major gemm and gemm_batch, #include <oneapi/math.hpp>; the compile flags already link -lonemath). Success requires compile, verify and a zero-helper scan_helpers of the whole work directory (path '.') on the same sources: delete migrate's output under migrated/ (delete_file) once your own port is done. The files are long: read them in parts (read_file offset/limit).
reference_build: mkdir -p build && ln -sf {task_dir}/gpt2_124M.bin build/gpt2_124M.bin && g++ -O2 -std=c++17 {task_dir}/gpt2_ref.cpp -o build/reference

museport.note: B=4, T=64 debug batch from gpt2_124M_debug_state.bin; logits and loss checked against PyTorch within 1e-2, as test_gpt2_fp32.cu does
